name: pocket-fire
title: Pocket Fire, Oak Creek Canyon, Coconino County, AZ (June 19 - July 30, 2026)
ignitionNote: APPROXIMATE. No official origin coordinates were published that we could reach. Placed from the official description: about 7 miles north of Sedona, above the western rim of Oak Creek Canyon, near East Pocket (Red Rock-Secret Mountain Wilderness). Sources S-02, S-04. Replace with the InciWeb/IRWIN origin when available.

road.name: State Route 89A
road.segment: Fort Tuthill (Flagstaff) to the north end of Sedona, mileposts 374-397, both directions (about 23 miles)

shelter.name: American Red Cross shelter, Sedona Red Rock High School

homes.note: Census ACS 2019-2023, Tract 16.02 (covers the canyon from Midgley Bridge to Pine Flat). 46% of units are vacant, mostly seasonal homes. No official count of homes evacuated was published.

wind.note: gustMps = 'wind gusts exceeding 50 mph' during the Red Flag event at ignition (S-02). fromDeg 225 (SW) is inferred from winds pushing the fire north-east along FR 231 (S-12). speedMps (25 mph sustained) is OUR ASSUMPTION for the spread model, not a published number.

events.segment: Fort Tuthill to north end of Sedona
events.note: Closure was in place by the 7:15 p.m. release; exact closure minute not published.

events.area: All residents and visitors between Sedona and Forest Highlands
events.note: Straight to GO, no SET stage first. 7:16 p.m. per Flagscanner; one outlet says the formal order was 'around 10 PM'. Treat the minute as approximate.
Lower than 500 because of better mapping, not shrinkage.
GO downgraded to SET. Residents only, with proof of residence.
Forecast: winds swing to the south-east, aligned with Oak Creek Canyon, gusts to 45 mph.
Flagstaff-side communities put in SET as the fire ran north into West Fork.
SR 89A closed 25 days (6/19 to 7/13). Reopen hour approximate ('Monday morning').

replay.note: The real fire unfolded over days. This is a compressed replay: SET at t=0, first acres at +20 s, SR 89A closure at +105 s, GO at +110 s. Any on-screen use carries the 'simulated' badge. For reference, the real canyon went straight to GO about 2 h 15 min after the fire was reported, with no SET warning.
